failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_SE,B, leakage
table: Chapter 3, Section 3.2.3 Failure Rate Model for Gaskets and Static Seals, Equation (3-7)
method: Base rate for random cuts, installation errors and similar causes, normalized to Navy 3-M field data, 2.4 failures per million hours, scaled here to per hour. Model lambda_SE = lambda_SE,B x C_P x C_Q x C_DL x C_H x C_F x C_nu x C_T x C_N (Equation 3-7). C_P = 0.25 for P_S up to 1500 psi and (P_S/3000)^2 above, with P_S = P1 - P2. C_Q = 0.055/Q_f for Q_f above 0.03 in3/min and 4.2 - 79 Q_f at or below. C_DL = 1.1 D_SL + 0.32 for seals and 0.45 (L/w) + 0.32 for gaskets. C_H = ((M/C)/0.55)^4.3 with M the Meyer hardness and C the contact pressure. C_F = 0.25 for f up to 15 microinch and f^1.65/353 above. C_nu = nu_o/nu with nu_o = 2 x 10^-8 lbf-min/in2 (Table 3-3). C_T = 1/2^t with t = (T_R - T_O)/18 for T_R - T_O up to 40 F and C_T = 0.21 above 40 F. C_N = (C_o/C_10)^3 x FR x N_10 with C_10 = 10 micron (Table 3-4).

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_SE,B, leakage
table: Chapter 3, Section 3.3.3 Failure Rate Model for Dynamic Seals, Equation (3-14)
method: Base rate of a dynamic seal, 22.8 failures per million hours, scaled here to per hour. Model lambda_SE = lambda_SE,B x C_P x C_Q x C_DL x C_H x C_F x C_nu x C_T x C_N x C_PV (Equation 3-14). C_P, C_DL and C_H use the static seal forms below 800 rpm or 600 ft/min and equal 1.0 at or above, while C_PV applies only at or above and is 1.0 below. C_F = 1.00 for f up to 10 microinch and 1/2^((10 - f)/38) above (Figure 3.17). C_PV = PV_OP/PV_DS with PV = (pi/12) x DP x d x V x k and k = 1.0 for unbalanced and 0.4 for balanced seals (Equations 3-13 and 3-15). Static seal forms: C_P = 0.25 for P_S up to 1500 psi and (P_S/3000)^2 above, with P_S = P1 - P2. C_Q = 0.055/Q_f for Q_f above 0.03 in3/min and 4.2 - 79 Q_f at or below. C_DL = 1.1 D_SL + 0.32 for seals and 0.45 (L/w) + 0.32 for gaskets. C_H = ((M/C)/0.55)^4.3 with M the Meyer hardness and C the contact pressure. C_F = 0.25 for f up to 15 microinch and f^1.65/353 above. C_nu = nu_o/nu with nu_o = 2 x 10^-8 lbf-min/in2 (Table 3-3). C_T = 1/2^t with t = (T_R - T_O)/18 for T_R - T_O up to 40 F and C_T = 0.21 above 40 F. C_N = (C_o/C_10)^3 x FR x N_10 with C_10 = 10 micron (Table 3-4).

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_SE,B, leakage
table: Chapter 3, Section 3.4.2 Failure Rate Model for Mechanical Seals, Equation (3-16)
method: Base rate of a balanced mechanical seal rotating above 800 rpm or sliding above 600 ft/min, 22.8 failures per million hours, scaled here to per hour. Model lambda_SE = lambda_SE,B x C_Q x C_F x C_nu x C_T x C_N x C_PV (Equation 3-16). C_Q = 0.055/Q_f above 0.03 in3/min and 4.2 - 79 Q_f at or below. C_F = 1.00 for f up to 10 microinch and 1/2^((10 - f)/38) above (Figure 3.17). C_PV = PV_OP/PV_DS with PV = (pi/12) x DP x d x V x k and k = 1.0 for unbalanced and 0.4 for balanced seals (Equations 3-13 and 3-15). C_nu from Table 3-3, C_T from Figure 3.16 and C_N from Table 3-4.

failureMode: C_P fluid pressure factor, P_S = P1 - P2 at or below 1500 psi
table: Figure 3.10 Fluid Pressure Multiplying Factor, CP
method: Constant branch of the fluid pressure factor in the static seal model lambda_SE = lambda_SE,B x C_P x C_Q x C_DL x C_H x C_F x C_nu x C_T x C_N (Equation 3-7) and in the dynamic seal model of Equation (3-14). Above 1500 psi C_P = (P_S/3000)^2.

failureMode: C_F surface finish factor, finish f at or below 15 microinch
table: Figure 3.15 Surface Finish Multiplying Factor, CF (for static seals)
method: Constant branch of the static seal surface finish factor in lambda_SE = lambda_SE,B x C_P x C_Q x C_DL x C_H x C_F x C_nu x C_T x C_N (Equation 3-7). Above 15 microinch C_F = f^1.65/353.

failureMode: C_T temperature factor, rated minus operating temperature above 40 F
table: Figure 3.16 Temperature Multiplying Factor, CT
method: Constant branch of the seal temperature factor (Equation 3-11) used in lambda_SE = lambda_SE,B x C_P x C_Q x C_DL x C_H x C_F x C_nu x C_T x C_N (Equation 3-7) and in Equations (3-14) and (3-16). For T_R - T_O up to 40 F C_T = 1/2^t with t = (T_R - T_O)/18.

failureMode: C_F surface finish factor, finish f at or below 10 microinch
table: Figure 3.17 Surface Finish Multiplying Factor, CF (for dynamic seals)
method: Constant branch of the dynamic seal surface finish factor used in lambda_SE = lambda_SE,B x C_P x C_Q x C_DL x C_H x C_F x C_nu x C_T x C_N x C_PV (Equation 3-14) and in the mechanical seal model of Equation (3-16). Above 10 microinch C_F = 1/2^((10 - f)/38).

failureMode: C_P fluid pressure factor, seal movement at or above 800 rpm or 600 ft/min
table: Chapter 3, Section 3.3.3 Failure Rate Model for Dynamic Seals, Equation (3-14)
method: The dynamic seal model lambda_SE = lambda_SE,B x C_P x C_Q x C_DL x C_H x C_F x C_nu x C_T x C_N x C_PV (Equation 3-14) sets this factor to 1.0 for fast seal movement, where C_PV accounts for the pressure velocity effect instead.

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_SP,B, fracture or loss of load
table: Chapter 4, Section 4.4.1 Compression Spring, Equations (4-5) and (4-6)
method: Base rate 23.8 failures per million hours, scaled here to per hour. Section 4.4.2 applies the same model to extension springs with all coils active. Model lambda_SP = lambda_SP,B x C_G x C_DW x C_DC x C_N x C_Y x C_L x C_K x C_CS x C_R x C_M (Equation 4-6), derived from lambda_SP = lambda_SP,B x (S_G/T_S)^3 (Equation 4-5). C_G = (G_M/(11.5 x 10^6))^3 (Table 4-2), C_DW = (D_W/0.085)^3, C_DC = (0.58/D_C)^6, C_N = (14/N_a)^3, C_Y = (190 x 10^3/T_S)^3 (Table 4-3). C_L = ((L1 - L2)/1.07)^3, C_K = (K_W/1.219)^3 with K_W = (4r - 1)/(4r - 4) + 0.616/r and r = D_C/D_W. C_CS = 0.100 for a cycle rate CR up to 30 cycles/min, CR/300 from 30 to 300 cycles/min and (CR/300)^3 above 300 (Figure 4.20). C_R = 1.0 with known corrosion protection and C_M = 1.0 with known acceptable quality control, higher values from experience (Sections 4.3.10 and 4.3.11). Where an S10 life is known, Section 4.2.1 multiplies it by 4.55 to obtain an average life.

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_SP,B, fracture or loss of load
table: Chapter 4, Section 4.4.3 Torsion Spring, Equations (4-11) and (4-12)
method: Base rate 14.3 failures per million hours, scaled here to per hour. Model lambda_SP = lambda_SP,B x C_E x C_DW x C_N x C_Y x C_L x C_CS x C_DC x C_R x C_M (Equation 4-12), derived from lambda_SP = lambda_SP,B x (S/T_S)^3 x C_CS x C_R x C_M (Equation 4-11). C_E = (E_M/(28.5 x 10^6))^3 (Table 4-2). C_DW = (D_W/0.085)^3, C_N = (14/N_a)^3, C_Y = (190 x 10^3/T_S)^3 (Table 4-3). C_L = (theta/0.667)^3 with theta the angular deflection in revolutions (Figure 4.15, while the equation key cites Figure 4.13). C_DC = (0.58/D_C)^3 (Figure 4.21). C_CS = 0.100 for a cycle rate CR up to 30 cycles/min, CR/300 from 30 to 300 cycles/min and (CR/300)^3 above 300 (Figure 4.20). C_R = 1.0 with known corrosion protection and C_M = 1.0 with known acceptable quality control, higher values from experience (Sections 4.3.10 and 4.3.11).

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_C,B
table: Chapter 5, Section 5.4 Failure Rate of Contactor Assembly, Equation (5-6)
method: Base rate 1.10 failures per million operations, stored here per operation. Failure is taken as contact resistance near twice the initial value. Model lambda_C = lambda_C,B x C_V x C_I (Equation 5-6) with C_V = (V_o/V_r)^0.75 and C_I = 3.50 (I_o/I_r)^1.14 for operating over rated voltage and current (Figures 5.3 and 5.4). It is a form of the general contactor model lambda_C = lambda_C,B x v^m x I^n (Equation 5-5).

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_C,B
table: Chapter 5, Section 5.4 Failure Rate of Contactor Assembly, Equation (5-7)
method: Base rate 3.60 failures per million operations, stored here per operation. Model lambda_C = lambda_C,B x C_V x C_I x C_PF (Equation 5-7) with C_V = (V_o/V_r)^0.75, C_I = 3.50 (I_o/I_r)^1.14 and C_PF = 4.0 (PF)^2 for power factor PF (Figures 5.3 to 5.5). It is a form of the general contactor model lambda_C = lambda_C,B x v^m x I^n (Equation 5-5).

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_C,B
table: Chapter 5, Section 5.4 Failure Rate of Contactor Assembly, Equation (5-8)
method: Base rate 2.5 failures per million operations, stored here per operation. DC loads arc more than AC loads. Model lambda_C = lambda_C,B x C_V x C_I (Equation 5-8) with C_V = (V_o/V_r)^1.33 and C_I = 4.20 (I_o/I_r)^1.30 (Figures 5.6 and 5.7). It is a form of the general contactor model lambda_C = lambda_C,B x v^m x I^n (Equation 5-5).

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_PO,B, internal leakage from wear
table: Chapter 6, Section 6.3 Failure Rate Model for Poppet Assembly, Equation (6-6)
method: Base rate 1.40 failures per million operations, stored here per operation, derived in Chapter 1. Model lambda_PO = lambda_PO,B x C_P x C_Q x C_F x C_nu x C_N x C_S x C_DT x C_SW x C_W (Equation 6-6). C_P = ((P1 - P2)/3000)^2 for P1 - P2 above 50 psi. C_Q = 0.055/Q_f above 0.03 in3/min and 4.2 - 79 Q_f at or below. C_nu from Table 6-6. C_N = (C_o/C_10)^3 x FR x N_10 (Table 6-5). C_W = 1.0 + F_L^2 with F_L the ratio of actual to rated flow. C_F = f^1.65/353. C_S = 0.26 (9000/S_S)^1.5 with S_S the poppet contact pressure. C_DT = 1.1 D_S + 0.32. C_SW = 3.55 - 24.52 L_W + 72.99 L_W^2 - 85.75 L_W^3 for L_W up to 0.34 in and 0.25 above. The valve total is lambda_VA = lambda_PO + lambda_SE + lambda_SP + lambda_SO + lambda_HO (Equation 6-1).

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_SV,B, internal leakage or sticking
table: Chapter 6, Section 6.4 Failure Rate Model for Sliding Action Valves, Equation (6-14)
method: Base rate 1.25 failures per million operations, stored here per operation. Model lambda_SV = lambda_SV,B x C_P x C_Q x C_nu x C_N x C_B x C_DS x C_mu x C_W (Equation 6-14). C_P = ((P1 - P2)/3000)^2 for P1 - P2 above 50 psi. C_Q = 0.055/Q_f above 0.03 in3/min and 4.2 - 79 Q_f at or below. C_nu from Table 6-6. C_N = (C_o/C_10)^3 x FR x N_10 (Table 6-5). C_W = 1.0 + F_L^2 with F_L the ratio of actual to rated flow. C_B = 0.42 for spool clearance B below 500 microinch and B^2/(6 x 10^5) above. C_DS = 0.615 D_SP. C_mu from Table 6-7. The valve total is lambda_VA = lambda_SV + lambda_SE + lambda_SP + lambda_SO + lambda_HO (Equation 6-2).

failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_HO,B, cracked housing
table: Chapter 6, Section 6.5 Failure Rate Estimate for Housing Assembly, Equation (6-15)
method: Base rate 0.01 failures per million hours, scaled here to per hour, best set from field experience. Model lambda_HO = lambda_HO,B (Equation 6-15).

failureMode: C_SW land width factor, land width above 0.34 in
table: Figure 6.11 Land Width Multiplying Factor
method: Constant branch of the land width factor in the poppet model lambda_PO = lambda_PO,B x C_P x C_Q x C_F x C_nu x C_N x C_S x C_DT x C_SW x C_W (Equation 6-6). For L_W up to 0.34 in C_SW = 3.55 - 24.52 L_W + 72.99 L_W^2 - 85.75 L_W^3.

failureMode: C_B spool clearance factor, clearance below 500 microinch
table: Figure 6.12 Spool Clearance Multiplying Factor
method: Constant branch of the spool clearance factor in the sliding action valve model lambda_SV = lambda_SV,B x C_P x C_Q x C_nu x C_N x C_B x C_DS x C_mu x C_W (Equation 6-14). Above 500 microinch C_B = B^2/(6 x 10^5).

failureMode: C_N particle size factor, most applications
table: Chapter 9, Section 9.3.2 Contaminant Multiplying Factor, Equation (9-19)
method: Printed as approximately 1.0. Factor of the actuator model lambda_AC = lambda_AC,B x C_CP x C_T in failures per million cycles (Equation 9-1). The base rate is lambda_AC,B = 10^6/N_O with N_O = 2000 (gamma F_Y/S_C)^9 cycles in the constant wear phase (Equation 9-2), wear factor gamma = 0.20 for materials prone to adhesive wear and 0.54 for materials with little transfer, and lubrication constants k1 = 15.4 x 10^3 for side load and k2 = 17.7 x 10^3 for axial load (Equations 9-4 and 9-6). C_CP = C_H x C_S x C_N with C_H = H_P/H_C and C_S = filter size in micron/10 (Equation 9-19). C_T = e^(4[1 - (25.2/T)]) for theta = 1200 K (Equation 9-23).

failureMode: C_N particle size factor, severe conditions with more and larger contaminants
table: Chapter 9, Section 9.3.2 Contaminant Multiplying Factor, Equation (9-19)
method: The text says the factor may be expected to approach 2.0 under severe conditions. Factor of the actuator model lambda_AC = lambda_AC,B x C_CP x C_T in failures per million cycles (Equation 9-1). The base rate is lambda_AC,B = 10^6/N_O with N_O = 2000 (gamma F_Y/S_C)^9 cycles in the constant wear phase (Equation 9-2), wear factor gamma = 0.20 for materials prone to adhesive wear and 0.54 for materials with little transfer, and lubrication constants k1 = 15.4 x 10^3 for side load and k2 = 17.7 x 10^3 for axial load (Equations 9-4 and 9-6). C_CP = C_H x C_S x C_N with C_H = H_P/H_C and C_S = filter size in micron/10 (Equation 9-19). C_T = e^(4[1 - (25.2/T)]) for theta = 1200 K (Equation 9-23).

failureMode: Failure rate lambda_CA
table: Chapter 10, Section 10.7 Failure Rate Model for Pump Casing
method: Estimated casing failure rate, 0.01 failures per million hours, scaled here to per hour. It enters the pump total lambda_P = lambda_SE + lambda_SH + lambda_BE + lambda_CA + lambda_FD (Equation 10-2).

component: Centrifugal pump fluid driver, axial flow impeller, closed or open impellers
failureMode: Base failure rate lambda_FD,B
table: Table 10-4. Base Failure Rates for Pump Fluid Drivers (λFD,B)

failureMode: C_BT brake type factor, drum type brakes

method: Brake type factor based on field performance data (Reference 20). Factor of the brake friction material model lambda_FR = lambda_FR,B x C_BT x C_RD x C_T (Equation 12-6).
